title: upfly undo --json: the result
description: The line upfly undo --json prints when it finishes: what it put back, or null when there was nothing to undo. A run that refuses, because a file changed since the run or another run is going, prints an error line instead (events.json) and changes nothing.

undone.description: The run undone, or null when no run was left to undo.

restored.description: Originals the run had removed, back in place.

reverted.description: Files whose references are as they were again.

removed.description: Files the run had created, gone again.

moved.description: Images the run had moved, back where they were: from is where each is again, to where the run had put it.

commit.description: The commit --commit made for that run, or null. It stays in the history, so the files undo put back show as uncommitted changes.

notes.description: Each a sentence: why there was nothing to undo, or what to do about the commit.
